description: Implement structured data (JSON-LD) and meta description fallbacks for Acrylicon WordPress multisite. Goal: Make Acrylicon visible in Google search results and AI Overviews for Norwegian industry flooring keywords.

userStories.title: Organization schema (sitewide)
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want to understand Acrylicon as a business entity so I can display it in Knowledge Graph and AI Overviews.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD Organization schema outputs in <head> on all pages via wp_head hook
Schema includes: name (AcryliCon), url, logo, description, foundingDate (1978), contactPoint, address (hovedkontor), sameAs (social profiles if any)
Uses production URL (https://acryli-28355.jana-osl.servebolt.cloud) as @id and url
Multisite-aware: outputs Norwegian content on blog 3, English on blog 1
Valid JSON-LD verified by extracting from page source and parsing with jq
PHP syntax check passes on all modified files
Implementation in new file: themes/acrylicon-2024/inc/schema-markup.php, required from functions.php
userStories.notes: Create inc/schema-markup.php as dedicated file for all schema functions. This is the foundation — later stories add to this file.

userStories.title: LocalBusiness schema for office pages
userStories.description: As a user searching for 'industrigulv Bergen' or 'gulvløsninger Tromsø', I want Google to show the nearest Acrylicon office with address and contact info.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD LocalBusiness schema outputs on each office (kontor) single page
Schema includes: name, address (streetAddress, addressLocality, postalCode, addressCountry), telephone, url, parentOrganization (references SEO-001 Organization @id)
Data sourced from ACF fields on kontor post type (read existing field names from the posts)
Outputs on both blog 1 (EN) and blog 3 (NO) with correct language content
4 offices should each have their own LocalBusiness schema
Valid JSON-LD, PHP syntax passes
userStories.notes: Check ACF field names on kontor CPT first. Fields likely include address-related fields. Use get_field() to source data.

userStories.title: Product schema for product pages
userStories.description: As a user searching for 'epoxy gulv' or 'akryl belegg', I want Google to show Acrylicon products with rich results.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD Product schema outputs on each produkter single page
Schema includes: name, description (from product_excerpt ACF field, stripped of HTML), brand (AcryliCon), manufacturer, category
Includes offers with priceCurrency NOK and availability (InStock)
Data sourced from ACF fields on produkter post type
Works on both blog 1 (EN) and blog 3 (NO)
12 product systems should each have schema
Valid JSON-LD, PHP syntax passes
userStories.notes: product_excerpt exists on 10 of 12 products. For the 2 without (Multi-Grip ID, TankCoating), fall back to post excerpt or title.

userStories.title: BreadcrumbList schema for all pages
userStories.description: As a search engine, I want to display navigation breadcrumbs in search results so users understand the site structure.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD BreadcrumbList schema outputs on all pages (not just frontpage)
Breadcrumb trail: Home > [Post Type Archive if applicable] > [Current Page]
For CPTs: Home > Produkter > {Product Name}
For pages: Home > {Page Name} (or Home > {Parent} > {Page Name} for hierarchical)
Uses correct URLs for each breadcrumb item
Multisite-aware: Norwegian labels on blog 3, English on blog 1
Valid JSON-LD, PHP syntax passes
userStories.notes: Check if Yoast already outputs breadcrumbs — if so, disable Yoast's and use custom to ensure multisite correctness. Use conditional blog_id checks for labels.

userStories.title: Article/CaseStudy schema for references
userStories.description: As a user searching for flooring case studies, I want Google to show Acrylicon's 100+ project references as rich results.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD Article schema (or CaseStudy if supported) outputs on each referanser single page
Schema includes: headline (title), datePublished, author (AcryliCon), description, image (featured image if available)
Includes about property linking to relevant product system
Works on both blog 1 and blog 3
Valid JSON-LD, PHP syntax passes
userStories.notes: referance_productsystem ACF field links references to products. Use this for the 'about' property.

userStories.title: Service schema for application area pages
userStories.description: As a user searching for 'gulvløsning næringsmiddel' or 'industrigulv sykehus', I want Google to show relevant Acrylicon application areas.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON-LD Service schema outputs on each bruksomrader single page
Schema includes: name, description, provider (references Organization @id), areaServed, serviceType
Works on both blog 1 and blog 3
Valid JSON-LD, PHP syntax passes
userStories.notes: bruksomrader (application areas) describe specific use cases like food industry, hospitals, etc.

userStories.title: Meta description PHP fallback via Yoast filter
userStories.description: As a search engine displaying results, I want every Acrylicon page to have a meaningful meta description instead of auto-generated garbage.
acceptanceCriteria: Filter on wpseo_metadesc that generates meta description when Yoast field is empty

Fallback templates per CPT: produkter uses product_excerpt (converted to prose), referanser uses title + product system, bruksomrader uses title + context, kontor uses address + region, industrier uses title, pages use excerpt or first 155 chars
Meta descriptions are 150-160 characters, Norwegian on blog 3, English on blog 1
Does NOT override manually written Yoast descriptions
Includes primary keyword naturally in each description
PHP syntax passes on all modified files
userStories.notes: See brainstorm doc for exact templates per CPT. product_excerpt is HTML bullet list — must be converted to readable prose. 2 products lack excerpt — fall back to title.

userStories.title: Verify and fix Yoast Open Graph output per blog
userStories.description: As a user sharing Acrylicon links on social media, I want correct og:title, og:description, og:image and og:locale for each page.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify Yoast Open Graph is enabled on both blog 1 and blog 3
og:locale outputs 'nb_NO' on blog 3 and 'en_US' on blog 1
og:site_name outputs 'AcryliCon' on both blogs
og:image falls back to a default image when no featured image is set
If Yoast OG is disabled or misconfigured, enable it or add custom OG tags via wp_head
Verify by checking page source for og: meta tags
userStories.notes: This may just require Yoast settings verification via WP-CLI. If code changes needed, add to schema-markup.php or create inc/social-meta.php.
